headline: Denied Harbor Homes' plan to demolish 10-12 and 14 Amherst Street and build a 32-unit apartment building, 4-2 vote.
summary: Members heard a presentation and public comment on a plan to demolish two buildings at 10-12 and 14 Amherst Street and build a 32-unit, three-story apartment building. Members voted 4-2 to deny the application.
decisions: Approved the September 28, 2026 minutes, 6-0-1, with Mr. Hirsh abstaining.
Denied the application for 10-12 and 14 Amherst Street, a 32-unit apartment building, by a 4-2 vote.

decision_evidence.quote: MOTION by Alderman Klee to approve the minutes as written SECONDED by Mr. Barrett Motion 6-0-1. Mr. Hirsh abstained

Alderman Klee made a motion not to approve the application as presented; Mr. Barrett seconded the motion. All in favor of denying the application. The vote was 4-2 in favor of the motion to deny the application. Mr. Hirsh and Chairman Vorbach voted against the motion.

decision_titles: 32-unit apartment building at 10-12 and 14 Amherst Street

HDC Meeting October 26, 2026                              Page 1 of 11 
 
NASHUA HISTORIC DISTRICT COMMISSION 
 
Monday, October 26, 2026, 6:00 p.m., City Hall, Room 208  
 
HDC Members Present: 
  
 Robert Vorbach 
 Christopher Barrett 
 Larry Hirsh 
 Paige Hultman 
 Alderwoman Patricia Klee 
 Marnie Gordon 
 Michelle Earnest (Alt) 
 
 Absent: 
 
 Lisa Law  
  
 Also present:  
 
 Scott McPhie, Planner 1  
 
Chairman Vorbach asked Mr. McPhie to take the roll call vote of members present 
 
Mr. McPhie, after the roll call, indicated there are seven members present, so there is a quorum   
   
MINUTES: 
 
September 28, 2026: 
 
MOTION by Alderman Klee to approve the minutes as written 
 
SECONDED by Mr. Barrett  
 
Motion 6-0-1.  Mr. Hirsh abstained 
 
MOTION CARRIED UNANIMOUSLY  
 
Mr. McPhie distributed to all commissioners: 
 
a. the criteria for voting  
b. Additional information on the 14 Amherst Street property 
c. All the letters and e-mails submitted by abutters for the project, which were sent earlier in 
the day by e-mail to commissioners, which were all in opposition to the project. 
 
NEW BUSINESS:
HDC Meeting October 26, 2026                              Page 2 of 11 
1. Harbor Homes Inc.-Henry Och, President and CEO (Owner); Jonathon Halle 
& Warren Street Architects, Inc. (Applicants) 10-12 Amherst Street (Sheet 68 
Lot 33)   Propo sed merger of lots located at 10 -12 and 14 Amherst Street, 
Demolition of existing buildings, and construction of a new 32 -unit, 3-story 
apartment building, Historic District overlay (HD), Downtown One 
overlay(D1), and Mixed-Use Overlay (MU), Ward 3. 
 
2. Harbor Homes Inc.-Henry Och, President and CEO (Owner); Jonathon Halle 
& Warren Street Architects, Inc. (Applicants) 14 Amherst Street (Sheet 68 Lot 
35) Proposed merger of lots located at 10 -12 and 14 Amherst Street, 
Demolition of existing buildings, and constr uction of a new 32 -unit, 3-story 
apartment building, Historic District overlay (HD), Downtown One 
Overlay(D1), and Mixed-Use Overlay (MU), Ward 3. 
 
 
The two addresses are part of  the same project and involve the same impacts, so only one vote 
was taken 
 
 
Alderman Patrica Klee indicated she is a member of the Historical Society, which is an abutter 
tonight, but has consulted with Nashua legal counsel, and  they indicated she does not need to 
recuse herself as there is no financial interest in the case and she has not made up her mind on the 
case and has no perceived notions ahead of the vote 
 
Mr. McPhie indicated he was a member of the Historical Society, but he would not be voting.  
 
  
 
Chair Vorbach opened the public hearing and  read the case s above and requested the applicant 
come forward and present their case to the Commission. 
 
Mr. Jonathan Halee, Warren Street Architects, representing the applicant, began his presentation 
and indicated the plan is to remove all the buildings on the lots and build a new structure that will 
be compatible with the surrounding buildings . He also explained that they are not here to argue 
the financial challenges of the site.  He indicated this was the third appearance in front of the 
Commission, and they had been working with Harbor Care for almost a year now. He indicated as 
part of the material provided, there was an existing conditions report provided by LM Associates 
providing an opinion of how badly changed the interior of the buildings was, and they currently 
would not qualify to be individually placed on the National Register, but as a Group of 
uninterrupted buildings making up all the lots in the Historic District, would be called a local 
National Register Historic District. The applicant indicated they have had conversations with the 
New Hampshire Department of Historical Resources as  well. He then expressed how LM 
Associates' report indicated the buildings had been changed over the years and one portion of the 
Port Cochere had been removed; therefore, the existing structures were not worthy of preserving. 
LM Associates said the buildings are significant for the dates of construction , but changes to the 
buildings in the fifties and sixties took all that away, therefore insignificant.  The two lots consist 
of 68-35 & 33 located at 10 -12 & 14 Amherst Street.  Once again, he repeated and reminded 
everyone that the buildings are in poor condition.  He then began to describe the characteristics of 
the interior of a historic building and explained how those characteristics do not meet modern 2023 
International building codes, which would include handicap accessibility,  therefore not allowing 
expansion of their existing use on site. A potential elevator would need to be built on the outside
HDC Meeting October 26, 2026                              Page 3 of 11 
of the building, which would alter the building's look and impact its current historical appearance. 
He said the firm has done a pretty extensive review of the Vernacular of the Surrounding buildings 
and decided that a new vintage-looking 1870s mansard roof style building would be compatible, 
replacing the two Victorian Italianate buildings of the 1850s . He believed this was what the 
Commission wanted from  the two  previous preliminary design reviews in front of this 
Commission. A six-foot-high fence would be added to reduce impacts to neighbors  south of the 
structure.  
 
Ms. Gould presented a Video to the Commission and audience members showing the proposed 
building that would better meet modern building codes and repeated  how the existing buildings 
are in poor condition. She described how the 3 Story Mansard roof was adjusted to look like two 
stories in some areas to meet the character of the neighborhood.  She described the various textures 
used to reduce a monolithic look . Ms. Gould indicated the parking for the property has been 
discussed, and it was determined that since the lots are within the Downtown Overlay District , it 
takes precedence over any underlying zoning district; therefore, no parking is required as both lots 
are located in that overlay dis trict. Aldermen Klee and Mr. McPhie agreed that was correct.  Mr. 
Halle indicated parking is not a big concern for their clients. Nine spaces are proposed.  
 
Mr. Hirsh asked how many units are proposed for this site. Ms. Gould said they are proposing 30 
units for the site, which will consist of three two -unit buildings and twenty-seven single units to 
house Veterans and other Harbor Care clients. Families with Children would occupy the two-unit 
apartments.  The facility will be recovery-friendly. 
 
Alderman K lee asked how many people are using the buildings currently. Ms. Gould then 
explained the Front Door Agency had two residents and two additional beds. Along with 5 
residents living in the14 Amherst Street building. 
 
Mr. Barret asked what the total occupancy of the current buildings was. Mr. Halle indicated twenty 
beds plus up to 25 persons total. Mr.  Barret said the new building would provide around 25 total 
units. He commented that it is a very beautiful building if located in the middle of a field , but the 
proposed building is way too big for that prominent corner.  I have a big issue with knocking down 
the existing buildings.   
 
Ms. Gordon then asked if a cost analysis was done for renovation s of the existing building. Mr. 
Halee said no formal analysis was done. He then referred back to the LM historic structures report, 
indicating that to do anything with the structure, you would need to gut the inside, and it would 
not satisfy what our program wants to accomplish today.  
 
Ms. Ernst indicated the new building looks nothing like the buildings around it, and the size and 
the scale are not appropriate for that intersection.  It looks nice but not there.  
 
Mr. Hirsh then asked whether the Commission did not already talk about scale the last two times 
you were here? Mr. Halee indicated yes informally.  Someone commented that no vote was taken 
at that time. 
 
Mr. Barrett then complimented River College's campus atmosphere and asked if they had looked 
into creating a campus atmosphere by utilizing the existing buildings.   
 
Mr. Halee said no.  He added that anything he would build on site would overshadow what is 
currently on the site.  The lot is very small, a postage stamp, and the costs would be very high.
HDC Meeting October 26, 2026                              Page 4 of 11 
Ms. Gordon asked if they had looked into placing the building back to make it fit in better with the 
district.   
 
Mr. Halee then expressed that his discussions with the Planning Department indicated a curb cut 
was not allowed off of Auburn Street. Planning pushed us not to change the curb cuts; this is what 
is there today, so stay with it. Planning also emphasized the need to work within the existing 
footprint. He spoke to the calculations utilized to determine the costs of not using the building 
footprint calculations. You have for example three million dollars calculated and you have 32 
units, all of a sudden you have $100,000 dollars of carrying costs.  
 
Ms. Gould added downtown zoning encourages no setbacks, so since these properties are in that 
overlay district, it meets the standards.  
 
Ms. Earnest indicated I am very sympathetic to the mission you have , but this is the Historic 
District and the building is not in character with the surrounding buildings, and if we allow this to 
happen it opens up a ver y dangerous precedent for others to request the same in the district. 
Alderman Klee then indicated her agreement with her colleague  
 
Ms. Earnest and complimented all the wonderful programs that Harbor Care does. She said her  
concerns are the massive size of the structure , but my number one concern is th e loss of these 
historical houses.  The HDC has jurisdiction over the outside appearance and the exterior of the 
house, but no jurisdiction over the inside of the house, and you can gut it if you want to.  
 
Alderman Klee added that the focus of the historic district, as long as she has been a commissioner, 
is to keep the history, so when you drive by, it stays in place.  She cited the example of a typical 
case where someone wanted to change the portico of a b uilding from what is there today, and we 
said no. Although it is rotting, we do not care; we want you to rebuild it. There was a building on 
the property that would not be saved, and we required them to rebuild it to the likeness of the old 
building.  Alde rman Klee then complimented the group again for their services but added that 
these buildings at 10-12 & 14 Amherst Street go beyond their visual appearance; they were part 
of what I call Nashua’s Civil War, when the community split up, and this area was r eferred to as 
Nashville. I know the Historical Society representatives are here, but you have to realize you are 
putting up a  big new building across from the Historic Abbot House that looks nothing like the 
other buildings in the neighborhood. It is such a drastic change, and I agree with my colleagues 
here.  If you presented a minor change to the existing buildings or adding something to the back 
of them I might have gone for that but although a beautiful building I do not see it happening in 
this location.  
 
Ms. Gordon said she is new to the board and this is the first time she has seen the proposal.  She 
brought up the fact that she has visited many historic Districts in her business travels, and many 
integrate compatible new buildings with historical buildings. She asked if this was the first time 
this proposal was presented to the Commission. Chair man Vorbach said yes, they had presented 
other proposals on a preliminary basis , but none formally for a vote. She suggested maintaining 
the fronts of the existing buildings and integrating them with something new in the back to 
maintain the appearance of the district.  
 
Mr. Halle said I think Lisa Masoulf (LM) , who is the Historic Preservationist , indicated the 
program we are trying to fit on the site would not work here  if we used the existing buildings . If 
the building is gutted, it would ruin what is historic inside of the house, and there is very little 
money to renovate in place.
HDC Meeting October 26, 2026                              Page 5 of 11 
Ms. Gordon said I am not saying renovate in place.  What you are proposing is completely different 
than what the current buildings look like.  
 
Mr. Halee said they did look at buildings within a one -block radius of the area and decided that 
this proposal would be appropriate. The program needs a three-story building profile and indicated 
there is just more proposed here than what the footprint allows so we did what we could do.   
 
Mr. Barrett said exactly that statement; that is what the problem is: it is just too big for what is 
there. I could see the design down by Greeley Park.   
 
Chairman Vorbach said he would argue with Commissioner Barrett's assessment about the 
footprint.   
 
Ms. Gordon indicated we understand that, as an architect, you are trying to maximize the space 
you need to perform your function, but keep in mind that, as a historic district, we are trying to 
follow our rules. Is it the idea  to create one big block like Monahan Manor ?  Your design is 
beautiful, but it does have that big block look.  How about jogging or more of a townhouse design 
instead of one big structure?   
 
Mr. Barrett cited a building like that would be more appropriate up to a lot line, such as the Citizens 
Bank building on Main Street. It's just not an appropriate building for the neighborhood.  
 
Mr. Halee added we could change the appearance of the Mansard by changing the paint color.   
 
Chairman Vorbach indicated he was very pleased with the presentation and the proposed building 
is far better than those normally proposed in a City that does not prioritize good architecture. He 
disagrees that the building design was not in character with the neighborhood because there was a 
Mansard roof building next to the Fire Station just down the street. He beli eves the building in 
question at 10 -12 & 14 Amherst Street is  no longer historic due to all the alterations made 
throughout the years. Unfortunately, not very different from many of the run -down homes on 
Concord Street in the Historic District that are thankfully being brought back to life.  He cited the 
other recent example of the run -down yellow Apartment building at 6 Canal Street that was 
brought back to life, and that was a good thing. The problem with maintaining older buildings is a 
real thing.  He reiterated again that he felt the building was in character and architecturally fits in 
the district  and said the Commission  will be dealing with this same scenario in the future. 
Regarding new construction , what standards do we set ? Unfortunately, located in the Historic 
District, there are many prominent features that are buried under vinyl or aluminum siding .  He 
added that he understands the rest of the Commission's comments, but being an architect trying to 
make their program work within these buildings is probably not possible. In closing, he said I will 
again emphasize that the contextual architecture of the building is one of the best I have seen in 
this city. 
 
Alderman Klee then asked the Harbor Homes representati ves how long they have owned the 
buildings.  They indicated since the early 1990’s . Ald. Klee said it is not that you just purchased 
the buildings and you were not aware you were in a Historic District.  They agreed no, they were 
aware. Alderman Klee said she has always been fair to allow the neighborhood in the historic 
District to reflect the surrounding buildings and cited the recent approval of vinyl windows on 
Manchester Street, but in this area, razing those buildings is too much of an impact. Current ly, 
there are two separate buildings on site ; your proposal , although is a mansard  roofs in the 
neighborhood, the new building  is still one big block and does not fit  in with what is there .  In 
terms of a new building, she has no problem with a vacant lot with no buildings or history on it to
HDC Meeting October 26, 2026                              Page 6 of 11 
allow such a building. What you are proposing is taking down two historical buildings that at least 
the City defines as historical buildings is not appropriate here.  Furthermore, you know this is a 
Historic District, and yes, your services are valuable, but to try to do something this drastic as 
removing these two buildings - that is what I have a big issue with. How is it any different from 
taking a big house on Concord Street and saying I want to knock this down so I can sleep more 
people there? I would be saying the same thing today to that proposal as you are proposing today. 
 
The question was then asked if the historic Buildings still  are classified as historic if they have 
changed over the years; therefore, we can take them down, as the proposed building is a lot nicer 
looking than the buildings that stand there now.  
 
Mr. Barret then explained that the 66 Concord Street House was in horrible condition, and he was 
in the house many times. The builder originally came  before us and wanted to knock all the 
buildings down and build new ones, and we said no, and he then worked with us to fix up the old 
house and complete his project. I just have a problem with knocking down those buildings in an 
area that prominent; it is not appropriate.  
 
Mr. Halee then responded that Lisa Mausolf, LM, said the significance of those buildings has been 
wiped out over time. He said she also had a conversation with the Department of Historical 
Resources and, yes, they said it had a diverse impact on the property, but said it was not an issue. 
We are being sensitive to the site because we are adding plaques to the new building telling the 
long history of the buildings that will be demolished that are there today. He added that they both 
agreed there was nothing significant about the buildings. It's very subjective.  
 
Mr. McPhie asked the Commissioners if the additional history of the buildings that was left out of 
the LM report and not part of the original NHDR report was read by all, as that adds quite a bit 
more detail to the site's history.   
 
Mr. Hallee said he is not disputing the history; that is why they are creating plaques to show what 
used to be on the site.  He explained other projects where they followed a similar method, such as 
the Rockingham County complex.  
 
Chairman Vorbach said there is no question these sites are historic , but from an architectural 
standpoint they have not been historically respected.  
 
Ald. Klee discussed the concerns of setting a precedent.  If we are willing to remove historic homes 
within this district and put up new buildings, we are setting a precedent; then we are going to have 
someone come before us in the future  and say this is going to cost me too much money, so we 
must take it down and build a new structure . We have always had some leeway with properties , 
but in your case, you knew you bought this property, and it was located within the historic district, 
and I assume it was  purchased at a great price at that time.  I am v ery concerned about setting a 
precedent.  
 
Mr. Hallee said they took great care in designing the building , and it is not low-end.  Alderman  
Klee responded that she was not concerned about materials , and her point was knocking down 
historic buildings in a Historic District, whether it be lore or reality; I am afraid if we allowed this 
there would be a bad precedent set.  
 
Ms. Gordon asked about zoning. Alderman Klee indicated it is currently zoned as it is , but if the 
City allows this and the new building w ere built, the City would allow the entire lot to be put
HDC Meeting October 26, 2026                              Page 7 of 11 
together and zoned under the district. Mr. McPhie said the overlay zone takes precedence, just like 
in a TOD zone.  
 
Mr. Halee said that this area is being rezoned by the City, not by us. He then talked about a four-
story building being allowed by right in the new zoning. He disagreed that the Historic District 
overlay trumps the other overlay. He indicated his client, Bangor Savings, wanted to do a similar 
project by adding a new Bangor Savings Bank on that lot at 1 Main Street, but they decided not to 
do so. You are going to encounter this conversation again.  The One Main Street property has been 
sold, and the building is still in place.  Chairman Vorbach asked if there were any further 
discussions.  Seeing None. He then called for anyone in the public who is opposed to the project 
to come forward.   
 
Speaking against the Proposal: 
 
Mrs. Paula Lochhead came forward and stated her name, indicating she is a Nashua resident and 
is on the Board of the Nashua Historical Society as well as the Chair of the Nashua Historical 
Society Historic Structures Committee . The  Nashua Historical Society is  a direct abutter and 
located just across the street. Dean Shalhoup, President of the Historical Society, was also present 
but did not speak.   
 
 
 
Mrs. Lochhead presented the detailed history of the 10 -12 Amherst Street building, indicating it 
shows prominent Italianate architectural features like the porte-cochere and the large roof portico. 
The building was constructed between 1850 and 1860.   Mr. George McQuest en, was the house 
builder. He owned a large lumber company and was a famous builder of wooden railroad bridges.  
He created a specialized beam to support them; one of those beams is signed by him and is located 
in the Mines Falls Gate House today. Mr. Roby was the next owner of the building, and he was a 
famous lumber merchant and a ship's mast supplier. Next, this was the location of the Lords I nn 
in the early 1900’s and the actual location  where the owners met to form the JF McElwain Shoe 
Corporation, whose factory is another historic Building in Downtown Nashua that was recently 
demolished.  She indicated the building was listed on the National Register of Historic Places.   
 
She then proceeded to talk about the 14 Amherst Street building.  This appears to have been built 
in the 1850- or 1860s, at a similar time frame as the previous building. The front of this building 
features unique Papyrus capitals; these columns pay homage to the earli est Egyptology craze in 
America, which occurred from 1850 -1870. These types of columns are very difficult to find in 
New Hampshire, and then said the structure is on the National Historic Register 
 
All these stories you just heard will be lost with the demolition of these properties. 
 
She then quoted from the Nashua City website. “The Historic District Commission shall have the 
power to accept, review, all applications for building permits for all properties situated within the 
boundaries of any Historic District established herein. I am sure, as Commissioners, you all have 
a certain trepidation to demolish buildings in the district and thereby set a precedent for future 
applicants who wish to expunge Nashua’s story.  I would also recommend to Harbor Homes that 
they do not jeopardize future federal grants by expunging Nashua's history. 
 
As you see from the letter presented to you by the Nashua Historical Society, we strongly oppose 
the demolition of these buildings and are actively preserving the buildings we have, as evidenced
HDC Meeting October 26, 2026                              Page 8 of 11 
by our continued care of the Abbot Spalding House that resides across the street from this proposed 
development. Thank You 
              
Speaking in Favor: 
 
No one 
 
Chairman Vorbach states we are ending the public hearing and opening the public meeting where 
we will begin additional discussions:  
 
Ms. Hultman said that, now that she has heard the presentation, she believes she will have to 
recuse herself from the vote as she is the President of the Board of Directors of the Front Door 
Agency and has an interest in renting at 10-12 Amherst Street. Alderman Klee repeated the 
criteria from Nashua’s Legal Department, saying if you have financial gain in that situation or 
feel you are influenced, you should recuse yourself. If there is any type of appearance like that..    
 
 
Ald. Klee did not realize these buildings were on the National Register. As Lisa Mausoff alluded 
to, the entire area is on the National Register but not the individual homes. Mr. McPhie indicated 
individual homes can be p otentially eligible for the National Register as well.  Obviously, some 
are more eligible; some are less. Alderman Klee then clarified the point, which would be 
contingent on how much work had been done.  Mr. McPhie agreed.  
 
Alderman Klee said again her f irst biggest issue was raising buildings in the Historic District 
equally as important as raising buildings located at this location in front of the Abbot Spaulding 
House and the War Memorial and all of the other surrounding historic buildings.  All of that talks 
about Nashua’s history. She cited the one Main Street example as the City was looking to acquire 
it, but they did not purchase the property because of the cost and because it's in the Historic District. 
I remember not voting in favor of that.  Mr. McPhie added a point of clarity: the brick building on 
Amherst Street you keep referring to is not in the Historic District.  Alderman Klee agreed that it 
is not.  She clarified that the brick building does border the Historic District, and if we allow 
demolition in the District, you are making the district just like the rest of Amherst Street when you 
drive down it. I am bringing up the Brick Building because it is so out of place with the other 
buildings around it. Mr. McPhie added, which is why they formed the Historic District in the first 
place.  Alderman Klee said exactly. She added, if we allow demolition, then we open up the area 
to look like what has happened on  the rest of  Amherst Street.  We have a very small Historic 
District in Nashua, and I am familiar with Chelmsford, Massachusetts, and just visited Darien, 
Connecticut. We have a lot of history in New England, but we are slowly obliterating it.  It bothers 
her to do so, as she wants to support Harbor Homes as much as possible, but this is not t he place 
for this building. 
 
Ms. Earnst wanted to note that all the  abutters' letters received that oppose the project  would be 
placed for the record. 
 
Chairman Vorbach added that both of these buildings unfortunately look shabby to me, and Nashua 
is notorious for such shabbiness of historical buildings.  He has always hoped that if you own a 
building, you should respect it and be proud of it and want to maintain it. If it's a building on the 
Historic Register, each should look like it should be on it; these two buildings do not look that way 
to me, and if they ever get to that level again, they will need to be provided with a lot of “TLC” to 
get there again.  He said that is sad to me.  What is our focus going to be: new Construction or 
restoration through repair and renovation over time?  We are in a good situation now, but we need
HDC Meeting October 26, 2026                              Page 9 of 11 
to discuss this further. He then indicated how nice the new building looks and stated the historic 
buildings on site now are shabby, so what direction do we want to follow? My opinion. 
 
Alderman Klee said While I do agree with you that the buildings look shabby, I compare it to many 
buildings in the Historic District that look shabby, but they are still standing, and we are not going 
to go around and say knock it down to rebuild.  Chairman Vorbach said Right.   We are going to 
say fix it and replace it; that is the goal of this Commission as long as I have been on it. When you 
talk about new construction, keep in mind it is on the backs of knocking down historic buildings 
to construct your new buildings.   Chairman Vorbach said Right. Alderman Klee then used the 
example that this is not like the vacant lot that was available for new Construction on Manchester 
Street.  This would be new construction on the backbone of raising two historical buildings. 
Chairman Vorbach agreed.  
 
Mr. Hirsh said, as a business guy who deals with construction on a daily basis, you are just trying 
to jam too much in a small area.  I would recommend you put your capital in a more appropriate 
situation.  
 
Ms. Hultman indicated she is the Board president of the Front Door agency that rents space at 
10-12 Amherst Street, so I might have to recuse myself. I apologize for not indicating earlier.  
 
Ms. Gordon then asked if we can make any recommendations as part of the motion as to what the 
applicant can do next.  Alderman Klee indicated we first have to make a motion to affirm or deny; 
then we can discuss recommendations for a future project. 
 
Chairman Vorbach said he will entertain a motion as presented for this project , approving it or 
denying it.    
 
Voting on this case: 
 
 Robert Vorbach 
 Christopher Barrett 
 Larry Hirsh 
 Alderwoman Patricia Klee 
     Marnie Gordon 
Michelle Earnest 
 
 
Alderman Klee made a motion not to approve the application as presented; Mr. Barrett seconded 
the motion. All in favor of denying the application. The vote was 4-2 in favor of the motion to 
deny the application.  Mr. Hirsh and Chair man Vorbach voted against the motion.  Mr. McPhie 
said the motion failed; Alderman Klee said no , the  motion passed. Mr. McPhie said I stand 
corrected. Motion passed.   
 
Then the applicant indicated on what grounds is the denial? Can you be more clear?   
 
Mr. McPhie reminded the commission to find the sheet he handed out earlier indicating the criteria 
they use under 190-22 A (2) for approval or denial.
HDC Meeting October 26, 2026                              Page 10 of 11 
DRAFT 
 
Alderman Klee listed the criteria.  
 
(2) Before passing on an application for a permit, and in reviewing the application, the Commission 
     shall take into account the purpose of this section and consider the following: 
 
(a)  
The historical or architectural value of the building or structure and its setting; and 
 
Alderman Klee said, as discussed before, you are taking down historical buildings. 
  
(b)  
The general compatibility of exterior design, arrangement, texture and materials proposed to be 
used in relationship to the existing building or structure and its setting or if new construction, to

She again indicated you are taking down a historical building to add a new building, which is the 
only reason you are creating new construction. She added that, while she knows that with the new

The general size and scale of new construction in relationship to the existing surroundings,

(d)  
Other factors, including yards, off -street parking space, location of entrance drives, sidewalks, 
extent and coverage of pavement, signs and landscaping, which might affect the character of any 
building or structure within the  Historic District  and any other factor which relates to the 
appropriate setting for such structure or grouping of structures; and 
 
She did not think they were violating anything in this particular case 
 
(e)  
The special character of the area including whether or not it is primarily residential or commercial; 
and 
 
She said she believes this is met  
 
(f)  
The economic activity of the building and the needs of that activity, and as it relates to the welfare 
of the community.

She said, obviously, you meet that criteria. 
 
She explained the first three criteria are not met, so you do not meet all the criteria of the ordinance.  
 
 
Mr. Hallee then asked what the next step to pursue is, as the Historic Districts only play an advisory 
role; is it a trip to the Planning Board?  Mr. McPhie added that your appeal will need to go to the 
Nashua Zoning Board  
 
A representative from Harbor Homes then a sked if they could come back with an alternative.  
Chairman Vornbach responded yes. 
 
Chairman Vorbach ended the Public Meeting
